title: All O(1) data structure — counts with O(1) max and min
label: multi
statement: Design a structure storing string counts: `Inc(key)` adds 1 (a new key starts at 1), `Dec(key)` subtracts 1 (at 0 the key disappears), `GetMaxKey()` and `GetMinKey()` return any key with the highest / lowest count, or `""` if empty. **Every operation must be O(1).**
provenance: Reported in a LinkedIn **Staff** loop (≈ Apr 2025, alongside Max Consecutive Ones III and Nested List Weight Sum II) and a Senior onsite (Nov 2025, codingkaro) — LeetCode 432, which is also on your LinkedIn-tagged list. Stage 2 (thread safety) is the follow-up every LinkedIn data-structure question ends on.

prompts.label: Check my design — no code
prompts.text: I believe keys grouped into buckets by count, the buckets in a doubly linked list in count order, and a map from key to its bucket node, so Inc and Dec move a key to a neighbouring bucket and max/min are the two ends — all O(1). Review my reasoning without giving me the implementation. What would break it?

prompts.label: Review, do not rewrite
prompts.text: Review my implementation for correctness and edge cases. Do not rewrite the code. List problems most severe first, each with the input that triggers it.

prompts.label: Race conditions
prompts.text: Now review this implementation for race conditions if multiple threads call Inc concurrently. For each race, give the interleaving that breaks it. Then name the smallest synchronization boundary that preserves correctness. Do not write code yet.

prompts.label: Tests that expose bugs
prompts.text: Suggest tests that could expose bugs in my implementation: boundaries, duplicates, empty and invalid input, and concurrency where it applies. For each, say why the expected value is correct.

prompts.label: Complexity check
prompts.text: What is the time and space complexity of each public method as written? Do not claim a bound unless every step achieves it.

prompts.label: Requirement change
prompts.text: The requirement changed: Concurrent Inc from many threads must lose no increments. List which members need to change and which do not, before writing any code.

learn.title: 1 · Problem
learn.md: Design a structure storing string counts: `Inc(key)` adds 1 (a new key starts at 1), `Dec(key)` subtracts 1 (at 0 the key disappears), `GetMaxKey()` and `GetMinKey()` return any key with the highest / lowest count, or `""` if empty. **Every operation must be O(1).**

learn.title: 2 · Clarifications
learn.md:
- Dec on a key that is not present? (No-op.)
- Ties for max/min: any key? (Yes.)
- Is O(1) amortised acceptable? (Each operation must be O(1).)

learn.title: 3 · Key insight
learn.md: A heap gives log n. O(1) works because counts only ever change by one: a key always moves to the bucket right next to its current one. Keep buckets in a linked list ordered by count, and the ends are the max and min.

learn.title: 4 · Approach
learn.md: I would say, before coding: "K."eys grouped into buckets by count, the buckets in a doubly linked list in count order, and a map from key to its bucket node, so Inc and Dec move a key to a neighbouring bucket and max/min are the two ends — all O(1)."

learn.title: 11 · AI usage strategy
learn.md:
- Make the design decision yourself, then ask the assistant to attack it.
- Delegate the mechanical parts only after the structure is fixed.

**Prompts for this question:**

- *Check my design — no code* — "I believe keys grouped into buckets by count, the buckets in a doubly linked list in count order, and a map from key to its bucket node, so Inc and Dec move a key to a neighbouring bucket and max/min are the two ends — all O(1). Review my reasoning without giving me the implementation. What would break it?"
- *Review, do not rewrite* — "Review my implementation for correctness and edge cases. Do not rewrite the code. List problems most severe first, each with the input that triggers it."
- *Race conditions* — "Now review this implementation for race conditions if multiple threads call Inc concurrently. For each race, give the interleaving that breaks it. Then name the smallest synchronization boundary that preserves correctness. Do not write code yet."
- *Tests that expose bugs* — "Suggest tests that could expose bugs in my implementation: boundaries, duplicates, empty and invalid input, and concurrency where it applies. For each, say why the expected value is correct."
- *Complexity check* — "What is the time and space complexity of each public method as written? Do not claim a bound unless every step achieves it."
- *Requirement change* — "The requirement changed: Concurrent Inc from many threads must lose no increments. List which members need to change and which do not, before writing any code."

learn.title: 12 · Common AI mistakes
learn.md:
- A SortedDictionary or heap — O(log n), not O(1).
- Leaving empty buckets in the list.
- Creating a new bucket in the wrong place when the neighbour has a different count.
- Dec on an absent key throwing.
